questions.question: Which is the most powerful river in the world in terms of its volume and extensive drainage into the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amazon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Amazon River** holds the distinction of being the world's largest river in terms of both discharge volume and drainage basin area, surpassing even the combined flow and basin areas of the Nile, Yangtze, and Mississippi Rivers.
 
• Additionally, it stands as the planet's largest drainage system by volume of flow and basin area.
 
• Throughout the year, the width of the Amazon River varies, with a range of 2 to 6 miles during the dry season (June to November) and expanding to up to 30 miles wide during the wet season (December through April).
 
• The Amazon River basin experiences substantial rainfall, particularly during the wet season, which significantly contributes to the river's formidable discharge volume.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Congo River**, spanning 4,700 kilometres (2,900 miles) in length, courses through west-central Africa. It ranks as the ninth-longest river globally and boasts the title of the world's deepest river, with recorded depths reaching approximately 220 meters (720 feet).
 
• **The Amur River, **also recognized as the Heilong River, stretches over 2,824 kilometres in length, delineating the boundary between Russia and China. It stands as one of Asia's longest rivers and is celebrated as one of the world's most extensive free-flowing waterways.
 
• **The Nile,** a significant river flowing northward in northeastern Africa, empties into the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.question: In the state of ______, the general direction of the Himalayas is from southwest to northeast.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh.**__

__
 
• Himalayas in the Darjiling and Sikkim regions lie in an east west direction, while in** Arunachal Pradesh** they are from southwest to the northwest direction. 
 
• Dihang River/Siang River is the name given to Brahmaputra River in Arunachal Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The Himalayas are classified into different divisions by Rivers flowing between them.

 
 

 
 
Punjab/Kashmir Himalayas

 
 
 
The part of the Himalayas that lies between the Indus River and Satluj River.

 
 
 

 
 
Kumaon Himalayas

 
 
 
The part of the Himalayas that lies between Satluj River and Kali River.

 
 
 

 
 
Nepal Himalayas

 
 
 
The part of the Himalayas that lies between the Kali River and Teesta River.

 
 
 

 
 
Assam Himalayas

 
 
 
The part of the Himalayas that lies between the Teesta River and Dihang River.

 
 
 

 
 
Purvanchal / Eastern Himalayas

 
 
 
The part of the Himalayas that lies beyond Dihang River valley.

 
Here the Himalayas bend sharply towards the south and spread along Indo-Myanmar Border.

questions.question: Which of the following is a mountain pass in the Pir Panjal range at a maximum altitude of 2832 metres that connects the Kashmir Valley in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir with the Outer Himalayas and the plains in the south?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banihal Pass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Banihal Pass **is a mountain pass across the Pir Panjal Range at a maximum elevation of 2,832 m (9,291 ft).
 
• It** joins **the Kashmir Valley in the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir to the outer Himalayas and the plains to the south.
 
• The road from **Jammu to Srinagar transversed Banihal Pass until 1956 when the Jawahar Tunnel was constructed under the pass.**
 
• The road now passes through the underpass and the **Banihal Pass is no longer used for road transport.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mana Pass is located **within the Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve, 47 km north of the town of Mana, India, and 52 km north of the Hindu pilgrimage town of Badrinath in Uttarakhand**.
 
• Bara-lacha la also known as Bara-lacha Pass, (el. 4,850 m or 15,910 ft) is a high mountain pass in the Zanskar range, connecting **Lahaul district in Himachal Pradesh to Leh district in Ladakh**.
 
• Zoji-La Pass is a high mountain pass that runs **through the Kashmir valley to Ladakh**.

questions.question: Which is the outermost layer of the Himalayan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shivalik Hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Shivalik Hills are a mountain range in the Outer Himalayas that extends about 2,400 km from the Indus River**__.

 __
 
• It flows west-northwest for an additional 1,000 miles from the Tisza River in the state of Sikkim, through Nepal, into northwestern India and northern Pakistan.
 
• Although only 10 miles wide in places, the range is a typical peak of 3,000 to 4,000 feet.
 
• The Shivalik is spread over a width of 10 t0 50 km and maintains an altitude of between 900 and 1110 metres.
 
• These ranges are composed of loose sediments and the valleys are usually covered with heavy gravel and alluvium.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Himalayas are considered to be the tallest and the youngest furrow mountain ranges or latitudes of the world.
 
• Their geological pattern is young, shaky, and flexible since the Himalayan uplift is an endless cycle, making them one of the tallest earthquake-prone areas or regions of the world.
 
• The outer Himalayas are also identified as **Manak Parbat** in historical times.
 
• The Himalayas consist of three parallel ranges, the Greater Himalayas known as the Himadri, the Lesser Himalayas called the Himachal, and the Shivalik hills, which comprise the foothills. 
 
• **Himalayan Ranges**
 
 
• A series of several **parallel or convergent ranges**.
 
• The ranges are separated by deep valleys from which a highly dissected topography [(of a plateau or upper part) is divided by several deep valleys].
 
• The southern slopes have steep slopes and the northern slopes have comparatively gentle slopes. [The ascent of Mount Everest is less busy than on the north side. But China imposes restrictions so climbers take the southern slopes from Nepal]
 
• Most of the Himalayan ranges fall in** India, Nepal and Bhutan**.
 
• The northern slopes are partly located in Tibet (Trans-Himalaya) while the western end lies in Pakistan, Afghanistan and Central Asia.
 
• The** Himalayas between Tibet and the Gangetic Plain** are a sequence of three parallel ranges.

questions.question: Which of the following mountains is formed as a result of the compression of tectonic plates, leading to the formation of large fold-like structures on the Earth's crust?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ural mountain in Russia.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Urals are among **the world's oldest extant mountain ranges.**
 
• For its age of 250 to 300 million years, the elevation of the mountains is unusually high.
 
• They are** formed as a result of the compression of tectonic plates, leading to the formation of large fold-like structures on the Earth's crust.**
 
• They formed during the** Uralian orogeny.**
 
• The formation occurred due to the collision of the eastern edge of the supercontinent Laurasia with the young and rheologically weak continent of **Kazakhstania. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It contains more than **1,000 different types of valuable minerals.**
 
• Since the 18th century, the mountains have contributed significantly to the mineral sector of the Russian economy.
 
• The region is one of the** largest producers of metallurgy** and** heavy industry production in the country.**
 
• The Urals are divided, from north to south, into** the Polar (or Arctic), Nether-Polar (or Sub-Arctic), Northern, Central and Southern parts.**

questions.question: ______ plains are formed due to the weathering of soluble rocks such as limestone and dolomite.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karst**__.

__
 
• **Karst plains are formed due to the weathering of soluble rocks such as limestone and dolomite**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Karst **is a distinctive topography in which the landscape is largely shaped by the dissolving action of water on **carbonate bedrock** such as **limestone and dolomite**, etc.

 
 
• When the rain falls through the atmosphere, it picks carbon dioxide which dissolves in the droplets.
 
• Once the rain hits the ground, it percolates through the soil and picks more carbon dioxide to form a weak solution of carbonic acid.
 
• The infiltrating water naturally exploits cracks in the rock.
 
• Over long periods, carbon bedrock begins to dissolve.
 
• Opening in bedrock increases in size and an underground drainage system begins to develop and allows more water to pass which further accelerates the formation process of karst.
 
• **Some of the landforms develop within the bedrock such as pools, sinkholes, doline, stalactites, stalagmites etc.**
 
• **​​Examples of karst topography:**
 
 
• Skocjan Caves, Slovenia
 
• The Puerto Princesa Underground River, Philippines
 
• Doline in the causse de Sauveterre, Lozere, France
 
• Li River, Guilin, China

• **Pidurutalagala **peak is also known as the Mount Pedro peak.

 
 
• It has a height of 2524 meters or 8281 feet above sea level.
 
• The peak is used as the central communications array of the Government of Sri Lanka and armed forces.
 
• It also serves as an important point in the country's radar system. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hkakabo Razi** is the highest mountain peak in Myanmar.
 
• **Kangkar Pünzum **is the highest mountain peak in Bhutan.
 
• **Mount Everest **is the highest mountain peak in Nepal.

questions.question: Which of the following regions in India is nicknamed as the storehouse of minerals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chota Nagpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Chota Nagpur Plateau** in India has earned the moniker **"storehouse of minerals"** due to its abundant mineral wealth.
 
• Comprised primarily of igneous rocks dating back to the Pre-Cambrian era, this plateau boasts a rich array of resources including mica, bauxite, copper, limestone, iron ore, and coal.
 
• Spanning across the states of Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, and Chhattisgarh, the Chota Nagpur Plateau sustains a populace whose primary occupation revolves around mining activities. 
 
• The Chota Nagpur Dry Deciduous Forests provide a habitat for a range of endangered species, including tigers, sloth bears, leopards, blackbucks, Asian elephants, and chinkaras. 
 
• Additionally, these forests harbour significant species of conservation concern, such as the lesser Florican and two species of hornbills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The expansive Deccan Plateau** in southern India is situated between the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats, generally delineated as the peninsular area south of the Narmada River.
 
• **The Western Ghats,** also referred to as the Sahyadri mountain range, sprawls across an expanse of 160,000 km², stretching approximately 1,600 km parallel to the western coastline of the Indian peninsula. This range traverses through the states of Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• **The Himalayas,** often simply called the Himalayas, form a formidable mountain range in Asia, acting as a natural barrier separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau.

questions.question: Where is Indian Institute of Skiing and Mountaineering situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gulmarg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **IISM **is a modern and the most popular ski training institute in our country which was established by the Ministry of Tourism, Govt. of India at Gulmarg in **1968** as a temporary project called **Gulmarg Winter Sports Project **(GWSP). 
 
• The initial project envisaged the development of Gulmarg as an international **ski resort** with the desired infrastructure and training ski guides to meet the requirement of tourists. 
 
• The ski hire shop was established along with a chairlift and a ski lift in the early 70s to promote skiing and adventure tourism amongst domestic and foreign tourists. 
 
• It also proposed to establish a cable car (Gandola) between **Gulmarg and Kongdori.** 
 
• The project was started in the borrowed huts of the Tourism department of J&K.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Jammu and Kashmir have 2 capitals: **Srinagar - The summer Capital, Jammu - Winter capital.**
 
• **Manoj Sinha** took charge as the Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir on the 7th of August,2020 at Raj Bhavan, Srinagar.

questions.question: Which of the following is a pass on the Pir Panjal Range?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banihal.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Banihal Pass:**

 
 
• Banihal Pass is a mountain pass across the **Pir Panjal Range at a maximum elevation of 2,832 m.**
 
• It connects the Kashmir Valley in the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir to the outer Himalayas and the plains to the south.
 
 
 
• The Pir Panjal ranges:
 
 
• It lies in the Inner Himalayan region, running from east southeast to west-northwest across the states of Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir in India, as well as Pakistan, Administered Kashmir in Pakistan, where the average elevation varies from 1,400 m to 4,100 m. 
 
• The Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, and Mahabharat ranges are a part of the Himachal range.
 
• Pir Panjal is the largest range on the Lesser Himalayas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zoji La Pass:**

 
 
• It is in the Zaskar range in the Indian union territory of Ladakh.
 
• The road route from Srinagar to Leh goes through this pass.
 
• It has been created by the Indus River.
 
 
 
• **Khardung La pass:**
 
 
• It is associated with the Ladakh mountain range in Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• The pass on the Ladakh Range lies north of Leh and is the gateway to the Shyok and Nubra valleys and serves as a motorable route from Leh in India to Kashgar in Central Asia.
 
 
 
• **Photu La pass:**
 
 
• It is on the Srinagar-Leh highway of the Himalayan Zanskar Range stand.
 
• This mountain pass is referred to as the highest point on the highway, going beyond the well-known Zoji La.

questions.question: ________ is the highest peak in the Eastern Ghats.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Mahendragiri **is the highest peak in the** Eastern Ghats mountain range.**
 
• It is located in the Indian state of Odisha and has an elevation of** 1,501 meters (4,925 feet) above sea level.**
 
• Mahendragiri is also considered a sacred site in Hindu mythology and is believed to be the place where Lord Parashurama, a Hindu deity, performed penance.
 
• The mountain is also known for its beautiful natural surroundings and is a popular trekking destination for adventure enthusiasts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** The Eastern Ghats is a mountain range that runs parallel to the eastern coast of India, stretching over 1,750 kilometers (1,087 miles) from West Bengal in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south.**
 
• The range is lower in elevation compared to the Western Ghats and has an average height of around 600 meters (1,969 feet) above sea level, with some peaks reaching up to **1,500 meters (4,921 feet).**
 
• The Eastern Ghats is a complex and diverse mountain range, consisting of **several hills, plateaus, valleys, and forests, with a variety of flora and fauna.**
 
• The range is home to many tribal communities, and several rivers originate from the Eastern Ghats.
 
• The Eastern Ghats is an important region for biodiversity conservation, with several protected areas and wildlife reserves, such as the** Simlipal National Park and Biosphere Reserve in Odisha, the Papikonda Wildlife Sanctuary in Andhra Pradesh, and the Kambalakonda Wildlife Sanctuary in Visakhapatnam.**
